title: Dental Caries: An Overview
subtitle: How it develops and what influences it

quiz.q: What process underlies caries?
options: Only a change in tooth color
Filling of the tooth with new cells
Demineralization of the tooth by acids
quiz.explanation: Caries is a demineralization process.

quiz.q: Which factor influences caries?
quiz.explanation: Biofilm and rapidly fermentable carbohydrates are among the main factors.

quiz.q: Why are fissures difficult to clean?
options: They are located in the pulp
They can be narrow and deep
quiz.explanation: Toothbrush bristles may not reach into narrow grooves.

quiz.q: Who makes the decision on caries treatment?
quiz.explanation: Diagnosis and treatment are determined after a dental examination.

quiz.q: What does prevention include?
quiz.explanation: Regular oral hygiene reduces the risk of caries.

quiz.q: What forms on the tooth surface every day?
quiz.explanation: Bacterial plaque must be removed regularly.

quiz.q: How often is toothbrushing usually recommended?
quiz.explanation: Twice a day with fluoride toothpaste.

quiz.q: How are the spaces between the teeth cleaned?
options: With dental floss or an interdental brush
quiz.explanation: A toothbrush does not reach between the teeth.

quiz.q: Which surface needs particular attention?
options: The grooves of the chewing surface
quiz.explanation: Plaque can accumulate in the grooves.

quiz.q: What determines when to have a preventive check-up?
quiz.explanation: The interval is set according to the dentist’s recommendation.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the periodontium?
quiz.explanation: Enamel is a layer of the crown; the periodontium is the tissue that supports the tooth.

quiz.q: To which root layer do the ligament fibers attach?
quiz.explanation: The fibers attach to cementum.

quiz.q: What is gingivitis?
quiz.explanation: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gingiva.

quiz.q: How does periodontitis differ from gingivitis?
options: The supporting tissues, including bone, are damaged
There is no difference at all
quiz.explanation: In periodontitis, the supporting tissues are damaged.

quiz.q: What should be done if the gums bleed?
quiz.explanation: The exact cause and treatment are determined by a dentist.

quiz.q: Which is the outer layer of the crown?
quiz.explanation: Enamel covers the crown and is the hardest tissue.

quiz.q: Where are blood vessels and nerves located?
quiz.explanation: The pulp is the soft, living tissue of the tooth.

quiz.q: To which layer do the periodontal ligament fibers attach?
quiz.explanation: The ligament fibers are anchored in root cementum.

quiz.q: Where is dentin located?
quiz.explanation: Dentin lies beneath the enamel and cementum, surrounding the pulp.

quiz.q: Why can enamel not regenerate on its own?
quiz.explanation: Enamel contains no living cells.

quiz.q: What is the chewing surface called?
quiz.explanation: The occlusal surface meets the opposing tooth during chewing.

quiz.q: Which surface faces the tongue?
quiz.explanation: The lingual surface faces the tongue.

quiz.q: Which proximal surface is closer to the midline of the dental arch?
quiz.explanation: The mesial surface lies on the side closer to the midline.

quiz.q: On which surface are fissures found?
quiz.explanation: Fissures (grooves) are located on the chewing surface.

quiz.q: Which surface faces the cheek?
quiz.explanation: The vestibular surface faces the cheek or lip.

title: Tooth Types and FDI Numbering
subtitle: The system for permanent and primary teeth

quiz.q: How many permanent teeth are there (including wisdom teeth)?
quiz.explanation: A complete permanent dentition has 32 teeth.

quiz.q: How many primary teeth are there?
quiz.explanation: There are 20 primary teeth.

quiz.q: What does the first digit of an FDI number indicate?
quiz.explanation: The first digit indicates the quadrant, one quarter of the dentition.

quiz.q: Which teeth mainly grind food?
quiz.explanation: Molars have a large chewing surface and grind food.

quiz.q: Which digits designate the quadrants for permanent teeth?
quiz.explanation: 1–4 for permanent teeth, 5–8 for primary teeth.
